title: Output preservation for related configurations
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite bit strings. Let $\mathrm{src}$ be a configuration of the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on input $x$, and let $\mathrm{dst}$ be a configuration of the universal machine associated with $c$ on the paired input encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$. If there are a natural number $p$ no greater than the length of the decoded machine's serialization, together with tape contents and head positions for the canonizer's work tapes, such that $\mathrm{dst}$ is the corresponding extended simulation configuration built from $\mathrm{src}$ and $p$, then the two configurations have the same output word.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{src}$ is a configuration of the decoded machine on input $x$
$\mathrm{dst}$ is a configuration of the associated universal machine on the paired input
There is a natural number $p$ at most the length of the decoded machine's serialization
There are tape contents and head positions for the canonizer's work tapes
$\mathrm{dst}$ equals the extended simulation configuration determined by $\mathrm{src}$, $p$, and those tape contents and head positions
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite bit
strings, and let $s$ be a configuration of the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on input
$x$. Let $t$ be a configuration of the universal machine associated with $c$ on the
encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$. If the checkpoint relation holds between $s$ and $t$, then
their output words are equal.
